title: Gurmat camps
hook: Gurmat camps teach young people kirtan, gatka and history
tomorrow: Fateh's new best friend is trouble. does company really matter?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a taunt at lunch, a hand on Simran's arm, and Gurveer's steady line: calm courage. He says he'll try the turban again on Monday. Meanwhile, an email landed.

Some forms are easy: name, date, sign. Some ask a question about your whole life in one checkbox. Next summer's gurmat camp has sent its counselor form, and the box says: returning? yes or no. Simran was a junior counselor this summer. A kid asked her on the last day if she'd be back. Now she'll be at college, move-in is right around camp week, and she's not sure she has another summer of this in her. She's been staring at the box for twenty minutes.
screen: `SOME FORMS ASK ABOUT YOUR LIFE.` → `RETURNING? YES / NO.` → `TWENTY MINUTES, ONE CHECKBOX.`

segments.voice: Gurmat means the Guru's teaching, and a gurmat camp is days of it, lived together. Kids learn kirtan, the singing of Gurbani; gatka, the Sikh martial art, with sticks and wooden swords; and the history of the Gurus and the Sikhs who came after. They eat langar together, and the older kids teach the younger ones. That's the part Simran keeps coming back to. On ang 72, Guru Nanak asks, in paraphrase: how do you recognize true company? It's where the One Name is spoken. A camp at its best is exactly that kind of company, the sangat, and the Gurus put learning inside it, not off on your own. Simran found out this summer that she learned more teaching a nine-year-old than sitting in a class. So what does the tradition give her today? Not a yes. It gives her a better question. Not, do I owe camp another summer? But, where will I learn alongside people next year? Camp might be one answer. A sangat near her college might be another. She doesn't check the box tonight. She writes the camp director an email instead, asking if a single week is possible.
screen: `GURMAT: THE GURU'S TEACHING.` · `KIRTAN, GATKA, HISTORY.` · `ANG 72: WHERE THE NAME IS SPOKEN.` · `WHERE WILL I LEARN WITH OTHERS?` · then, large: `LEARNING TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Make a small plan. Name one thing you'd like to learn alongside other people this year. Name what's most likely to get in the way. Then name the one step that gets around it, and sit with that step in mind.
Gurmat camps. Days of kirtan, gatka and Sikh history, where young people learn the Guru's teaching together.
Learning together: the question isn't whether you owe it, but where you'll find it next. That's today.
